cards.text: We're in the book of Jeremiah, friend, right after a long stretch about idols that can't even walk (Jeremiah 10:5). Now the passage turns to the people of the land, who are living under siege.

cards.question: The people living under siege get their first order. What are they told to do?

answers.text: Gather up their belongings from the land
Rebuild the walls around their city
Open the gates to the enemy army

cards.text: Pack your bags, friend, which is more than I got when the Millers slid me into the back of their junk drawer! Then the LORD speaks, and He says why.

cards.question: The LORD says He'll sling the people out of the land at this time.
The LORD says He'll bring distress on the people of the land so that they may be ___.

cards.text: Then it gets personal. The passage says, "Woe to me because of my brokenness; my wound is grievous!"

cards.question: Right after crying woe over a grievous wound, what does the passage say about that wound?

answers.text: It is my sickness and I must bear it
Someone else caused it and must fix it
It will heal on its own before long

cards.text: Now the picture is a tent, destroyed, with ALL its ropes snapped. I think this one hurts.

cards.question: In this picture of a destroyed tent, the sons are still close by, ready to help put it back up.

cards.text: The passage says why: the shepherds have become senseless, and they do not seek the LORD. That's a tour guide who REFUSES to look at the map.

cards.question: Because the shepherds don't seek the LORD, they have not prospered, and all their ___ is scattered.

cards.text: Then, LISTEN! The sound of a report is coming, a great commotion, the kind of noise that makes you freeze in bed at 2 a.m.

cards.question: Where is this great commotion coming from?
When the commotion arrives, the cities of Judah will be left full and thriving.

cards.text: Judah's cities will be a desolation, a haunt for jackals. When the jackals move in, friend, that neighborhood is NOT on the way up.
Then the passage turns from the warning and talks straight to the LORD.

cards.question: Talking straight to the LORD, the passage says that no one who walks directs his own steps.

cards.text: Then comes a request for the LORD's correction, on PURPOSE! Friend, I flinch when somebody just says, "Can I give you a little feedback?"

cards.question: The prayer asks the LORD for correction. How does it ask Him to correct?

answers.text: Only with justice and not in anger
Quickly so that it will soon be over
Privately and away from the people

cards.question: The prayer says correction in the LORD's anger would bring the one praying to ___.

cards.text: Then the prayer turns toward the nations that do not acknowledge the LORD, the families that do not call on His name.

cards.question: The prayer asks the LORD to pour out His ___ on the nations that do not acknowledge Him.
Why does the prayer ask the LORD to pour out wrath on those nations?

cards.text: The prayer calls God's people Jacob, after the man whose sons became the tribes of Israel (Genesis 49:28). Those nations have consumed him, finished him off and devastated his homeland.
